card.name: Chatty web-text sentence turns
card.fires_on: Sentence-ending periods and short linking words in casual, friendly web writing, where a reader is addressed directly (invitations to comment, reassurance, thanks).

modes.label: Period before an invitation
modes.description: A full stop that ends a sentence just before the writer invites comments or shares.
modes.example: discuss those ideas with one another<<.>> Have a novel take or think we left

modes.label: Casual connectors and asides
modes.description: Short words such as Which, So, Also, Thanks or might that begin or continue a conversational sentence.
modes.example: I don’t want our class to be like this.<< So>> let’s talk afterwards about ways I can

modes.label: Reassurance to reader
modes.description: Words in a friendly address to the reader, such as reassurance or a simple statement about free accounts.
modes.example: New to Typophile? Accounts<< are>> free, and easy to set up.

card.writes: It lowers the chance of a period-like ending and raises exclamation marks, giving a cheerful tone.
card.plain: It marks friendly, chatty web writing where the author speaks to the reader, and pushes the text toward an upbeat exclamation.
